newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end higher in late buying.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end higher in late buying.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended higher in moderate trading on Wednesday after it recovered from earlier profit taking through a late burst of buying, traders said.
Interest in certain big- and medium-capitalised stocks such as Telkom, Citra Marga, Sampoerna, Daya Guna Samudera and Multipolar in late trade helped push up the index, they said.

The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.84 points, or 0.28 percent, to close at 662.21 points after touching a high of 663.04 points in the morning session. Gainers outpaced losers 55 to 41, with 77 issues unchanged.

Brokers said the market was likely to be mixed on Thursday, with some counters, including banking stocks, undergoing a technical correction after recent gains while fresh buying was likely to be seen on big-capitalised stocks.
"Some fund managers will continue buying for their 1997 portfolio. Their interest will be well spread but firstliners will remain their main target," a foreign broker said.
Heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 4,275 on 4.5 million shares after touching a high of 4,300 rupiah on active buying due to its fundamentals, brokers said.
Fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudera rose 175 rupiah to 3,025 on about three million shares on fresh buying boosted by the perception that its price was relatively low, brokers said.
Retail and technology based services firm Multipolar was up 50 rupiah to 1,725 on 5.1 million shares.
Brokers attributed the rise to its announcement to open a second Wal-Mart store in North Jakarta, coupled with its plan to take a controlling 50.1-percent stake in retailer Matahari.
Multipolar announced on December 23 it had been granted an unconditional and irrevocable option from holding company PT Matahari Putra Prima to buy a 45 percent stake in Matahari.
It had also initiated a tender offer to buy a further 5.1 percent stake in Matahari. Multipolar said it would finance the investment through a proposed rights issue in May or June.
Multipolar had said its tender offer was subject to approval at an extraordinary shareholders meeting on January 30.
Secondary agribusiness firm Sierad Produce topped the active list with 10.1 million shares changing hands, but its price remained unchanged at 850 rupiah.
Brokers said it was actively traded because it's prices was considered to be low.

Bank Pikko, which debuted on the exchange on Wednesday, was actively traded with 9.3 million shares changing hands. It rose to 1,000 rupiah before easing to 925 rupiah by the lunchbreak. It closed at 900 rupiah, against an offer price of 800 rupiah.
